statement: No LAN match on the played build (6a30b4c9) has a record from two real PCs: its only LAN records are nine rows with the second PC simulated inside one program, and the real two-PC logs kept are from two older builds.
cost_basis: estimate, no comparable: the work is Orb and Orb 2 playing five matches per mode and Netcode reading the logs
risk: The 2026-11-07 logs show a deepest rollback of 20 and Orb reported stutter; the tuning made since has never been measured on two real PCs.

statement: An outside tester could not set up LAN without help: the folder is built on the hosting PC with that PC's address written into the shortcuts, needs an administrator firewall step, runs an unsigned Windows program, and its own words allow only Orb and Orb 2 to play.
cost_basis: docs/ep/proposals/co-op-2v2.md:36 puts one LAN co-op piece with what a human needs at about 5.5M tokens; a menu-started LAN with finding the other PC is of that order
risk: If LAN is promised to outside testers, finding the other PC and the firewall step are new work with no design page yet.
orb_question: Does LAN stay with Orb and Orb 2 only for Alpha? Recommended: yes; outside testers get the solo and same-PC modes.

statement: There is no LAN build for Linux or the Steam Deck and no Windows-against-Linux match has ever been run, so cross-platform LAN at Alpha is unproven and today impossible.
risk: The sim's own maths has matched one set of expected results on Windows (local gates) and Linux (CI) only with the editor program, not with two exported builds playing each other.
orb_question: Should a Windows PC be able to play a Steam Deck over LAN at Alpha? Recommended: no, Windows to Windows only; run one no-network comparison between a Windows PC and a Deck to keep the door open.

statement: A PC that falls silent is declared gone after 8 seconds, not the 5 seconds X-08 proposes, and no pulled-cable test on two real PCs is on record.
cost_basis: estimate, no comparable: one constant or one criterion number, plus one real pulled-cable trial
risk: The check drives the drop with a 1-second limit and a simulated silence, so the shipped 8-second path and a real cable pull are untested; how soon the link itself reports closed is not evidenced.

statement: Every LAN status except a dropped PC (waiting, could not connect, could not start, out of step, match over) is shown only in the window's title bar, and a detected state mismatch writes no report of its own.
risk: A full-screen or Deck player sees no title bar, so a failed start or a mismatch would look like a frozen or normal game.

statement: The report folder from both PCs has never been made from a real LAN save, and its shortcut needs Node and this repository at a fixed path on the main PC plus a hand copy of the second PC's files.
cost_basis: estimate, no comparable: the first real save decides whether any field name differs (docs/tools/lan-report.md:33)
risk: X-08 is measured from this folder; if the first real save does not fit the agreed shape the measurement fails on the day.

statement: LAN play reaches the game only through text patches the kit makes to a scratch copy of two game files, and neither the kit nor the patched game's real window, menu and pads are run by CI.
cost_basis: estimate, no comparable; shares its work with F-MODES-04
risk: Any edit to the patched lines stops the kit, which is found only when someone next builds a LAN folder.

statement: A replay carries a hash of its data, its format and its input version but no build id, so a replay from a build with the same data and different code is run and fails at a checkpoint instead of being refused with a plain message.
risk: A LAN save keeps the build's commit beside the replay, and Tools' clip tool refuses a wrong commit, but nothing inside the game or the replay format does.

statement: LAN 2v2 has been played on two real PCs only in its team form and only on the 2026-11-07 build; the apart form has no real two-PC record on any build.
cost_basis: estimate, no comparable: play time only

statement: The handshake refuses a proposed input wait above 8 ticks but not a negative one, which by the code leaves this PC on Waiting for ever with no failure message (traced in code, not run).
risk: Private home network only, so the harm is a stuck start, not a crash.

statement: The LAN link is plain, unencrypted ENet, which is acceptable on a home network and must change before any internet play.
The corrective plan's row for hardening the LAN link has an empty status cell although the delay cap, the packet checks and the dropped-PC handling are in the code and in CI.
cost_basis: estimate, no comparable: one line of a record

statement: The determinism lint has no rule for the engine's pow, exp or log, so a future bare use in the sim would pass it; none is in the sim today.
risk: These functions can differ between platforms' maths libraries, which is the cross-platform case Alpha adds.

statement: The Web export preset does not leave out the network folder, so the browser build's pack carries the unreached network scripts, including 26 test scripts.
risk: Owner picked by charter: export_presets.cfg has no owns line.

statement: Groundwork for online play (a spectator, a seat take-over proposal, a rollback bench that estimates a phone) sits in the network folder with CI time spent on it but no Alpha use.
The rollback, state-mismatch, transport, handshake and two-program ENet checks, each with a deliberately broken control run, pass in CI on Linux on a commit whose game code is the played build's.

The corrective plan's hardening is in the code and tested: a proposed wait above 8 ticks fails the handshake, every game packet is checked and dropped whole if bad, and a gone PC's fighter passes to the computer with an on-screen banner.
Two real PCs have played LAN matches with every state check matching: 690 checks on both PCs' logs on 2026-11-07 and 718 on the main PC's log on 2026-11-08, with no out-of-step line in any kept log.

The played build's LAN folder ran nine in-program rows (1v1, 2v2 apart, 2v2 together, at home-network and 120 ms links) with every state check matched and no script error, and its packed data equals the solo build's.
Two different processors (both 64-bit Windows PCs) computed the same seeded match with no network, agreeing on all 90 lines of the two-PC check.
The sim's own maths is enforced: the determinism lint and its self-test run in CI over the four sim folders, its allow list is empty, and the nightly native-against-web comparison passes.

The LAN folder is held to the home network: the kit refuses public and virtual-adapter addresses, the host accepts callers from its own /24 only, the firewall rule is one program, one UDP port and one subnet with a removal script, and the address stays out of the log.
Each PC saves the match with its replay, checkpoints and the build's commit at the end, at each pause, on closing and on a one-press report (F9, or View and RB), and CI plays saved matches back.
Two PCs on different data, setup, seed or protocol version cannot start a match: the handshake compares a key that includes the data hash and fails on both sides with a reason.
The LAN kit locks the reduce-flashing setting on and stops if it did not lock or if the capture hook is on.
LAN is the only network mode in the code: the only sockets opened under the network folder are ENet's on UDP port 47100, and Orb's record puts online play after launch.
